title: AID Protocol v2 — Curator
$comment: producer: Curator (utility, after C3), consumers: [C4, GUI]
description: Artifact emitted by the Curator utility (run after C3) containing remediation proposals for findings that cannot be auto-resolved, with status tracking per proposal.

allOf.$comment: extends aid-protocol-v2.schema.json envelope (reference only — not a resolved $ref)

curator.$comment: enforced — minimal payload; full schema defined in owning phase

proposal_status.$comment: E-057-2_2 Step 1 — vocabulary for whether Curator had a complete input set (audit-report.json) to work from

audit_report_ref.$comment: E-057-2_2 Step 1 (L1 fix) — sha256 of the CONTENT of the audit-report.json Curator actually consumed (not head_sha, which only proves same-commit); same pattern convention as audit-report.schema.json's input_manifest_hash. aid-fsm.sh done-advance recomputes this hash and blocks release on mismatch (sequencing proof).

adjudications.$comment: IMP-468 (D5): formal per-finding adjudication of audit-report.json's findings[]. A bare curator.blocking_findings:false never resolves a raw Auditor blocker on its own — every critical|high finding needs a matching entry here, bound to THIS exact audit report/candidate/run (enforced by aid-plan-fsm.sh _pfsm_finalize_review, plan-final boundary only). Structural shape only here; the exact-binding/completeness/disposition-legality enforcement lives in the runtime check, not this schema.

evidence_ref.$comment: public-safe evidence reference (e.g. a commit sha, a file path + line, or a durable receipt ref) — never a raw session id, absolute path or free-text transcript
